title: LifeOS desktop workspace
question: Choose the workspace character. All directions keep overview-first navigation and Work's table with an adjacent inspector; none copies VOLT.

options.label: Operations desk
options.thesis: An overview of actionable exceptions leads into a precise monthly working register.
options.viewport: Labeled navigation at left; overview groups Work, Money, and Habits by actual state. Work keeps month controls and compact totals above a dominant table, with record inspection at right.
options.risk: Overemphasizing exceptions could manufacture urgency; only existing factual states qualify.

raised.raise: Each pane owns a complete job and a clear boundary; no nested decorative containers.
State distinctions stay precise without spreading accent color across ordinary data.
Overview summaries cross-check domain records and retain stable reading positions; no gauges or invented trends.
Selection, focus, edit, and disabled states remain unmistakably different; no retro graphics.
Record actions belong to the pane they affect, with destructive actions isolated; no code-editor styling.
Overview-to-record navigation preserves orientation and selected context; no spatial chart metaphor.

options.label: Native records workbench
options.thesis: A restrained, familiar application frame makes the records and their actions the center of attention.
options.viewport: A compact overview offers meaningful domain summaries and direct entry points. Work opens into a month toolbar, numerical summary, large record table, and persistent inspector with explicit View and Edit states.
options.risk: Familiar desktop grammar is deliberately conventional; poor execution could become a generic administration screen.

options.label: Cloud quarry
options.thesis: Treat domain records as discrete blocks that can be inspected and assembled.
options.viewport: Sectioned record blocks place summaries above source records.
options.case: Loses audience identification and product clarity: constructive gestures do not match persisted record workflows.
options.kept: Complete pane ownership and structural boundaries, not its imagery.
options.risk: A physical construction metaphor would obscure ordinary record actions.

options.label: Cloud edge
options.thesis: Distinguish subtle evidence states through narrow spectral edges.
options.viewport: An airy evidence comparison surrounds selected records.
options.case: Loses both axes: expansive observation space and spectral states work against compact record operations.
options.kept: Precise state distinction without excessive accent use.
options.risk: Would recreate the spacious website character the owner rejects.

options.label: Night-flight instruments
options.thesis: Give each domain a stable instrument in a cross-check overview.
options.viewport: Fixed instrument positions summarize domain state before opening records.
options.case: Loses both axes: LifeOS is not live telemetry, and gauge geometry reduces space for records.
options.kept: Stable positions and explicit reconciliation between summary and records.
options.risk: Would copy the control-room aesthetic rather than improve the working model.

options.label: One-bit desktop
options.thesis: Use a literal early desktop with overlapping record windows.
options.viewport: Independent windows contain the overview, register, and selected record.
options.case: Loses both axes: retro presentation and window management distract from the selected fixed-pane workflow.
options.risk: A nostalgic skin would substitute style for professional utility.

options.label: Developer console
options.thesis: Use persistent graphite panels with local actions and isolated destructive controls.
options.viewport: Navigation, record table, and inspector tile a dark working surface.
options.case: Loses both axes against the task-specific desk: developer-tool identity is unrelated to personal reconciliation, and syntax-like signals add no clarity.
options.kept: Pane-local actions and deliberate isolation of destructive operations.
options.risk: Could turn LifeOS into an IDE imitation instead of a personal tool.

options.label: Star atlas
options.thesis: Navigate linked records through matched overview and detail coordinates.
options.viewport: A spatial overview links into selected detail plates.
options.case: Loses both axes: shifts are calendar records, not spatial objects; pan-and-zoom adds an unnecessary navigation model.
options.kept: Preserve orientation and selection across overview and detail.
options.risk: Would invent a visualization with no genuine task justification.

canonCard.label: Standard business dashboard
canonCard.thesis: Use conventional dashboard summaries and a familiar data-management workspace.
canonCard.viewport: Summary panels introduce domains; Work presents a toolbar, table, and adjacent inspector.
canonCard.risk: Generic dashboard patterns may preserve the website-like experience unless operational continuity is enforced.
